ops.title: Mixed-era trust-gate witness cannot tell 'gated' from 'mechanism absent'
ops.description:
Found by the Lane B closing refuter, defect 5 (attack D). Evidence-strength, not exploitable.

ci/mixedera/peers_test.go:294 witnessPreambleTrustGate files present when the strict daemon still
holds its socket after a relayed preamble. That is equally the signature of no inbound preamble
handling at all — the precut era own state.

Proven: deleting the inbound preamble dispatch entirely leaves the matrix printing
drain-preamble-trust-gate | PROVEN (cut). Only the sibling drain-preamble row failed, so the run
was red overall — no shippable tree greens the row without the mechanism. The row borrows all its
discrimination from the neighbouring drain-preamble claim in the same case, and nothing frozen
records that dependency.

The framework already bounds this in its own godoc
(TestEveryRegisteredWitnessBranchesOnWhatItWasHanded: "A branch is a lower bound on observation,
not a proof of it"), so this is the documented limit of a witness rather than a hole in the
harness.

Second, smaller: peers_test.go:309 hardcodes "the strict %s daemon" in the filed evidence string
and the witness never observes strictness. Attack C2 filed "the OS reaped the strict cut daemon"
for a daemon started without -strict. That string is what a human reads out of the job summary.

What survives adversarially: attacks B (bypass trust.Verify), C (drop -strict), and F (file the
evidence from the wrong witness) all go red, so the site/witness binding itself is unforgeable.

ops.text: Either the witness discriminates mechanism-absent, or the frozen record names its dependency on drain-preamble
peers_test.go:309 evidence string asserts only what the witness observed
